Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to deeply shake'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'bouleversé').

examples.text: Cette annonce a bouleversé toute l'agence.
examples.trans: This announcement shook the whole agency.

examples.text: Votre émotion a bouleversé la salle!

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'deeply shaken'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Pourtant, je me sens complètement bouleversé.

meanings.note: determiner: ce soir = tonight, cette semaine = this week
pronoun: c'est = it is; tout ce que = all that

meanings.note: Said to encourage someone. Masculine noun formed with the suffix '-age' (from Late Latin '-aticum') denoting an action, state, or collection. Standard masculine noun meaning 'courage, bravery'.

meanings.en: bon courage!: good luck!, hang in there!

meanings.note: D' before a vowel. Core French preposition meaning 'of', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

Fier de = proud of. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'proud'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le honneur', plural 'les honneurs') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'honor'.
